else.text: Ah! The unlicensed visitor. Excellent timing. Do stand behind the tape. Yes, I brought tape.
Today is a demonstration. The mountain is going to be bound, tagged and put on a very handsome spreadsheet.
Pryce sets a grey disc on the summit cairn. It has a barcode and a small green button.
This is a Wardstone. It listens to the old stones and tells them to be quiet. It's a one-button solution.
Hang on. Hang on. Is this actually safe? I'm streaming. If something goes wrong I'll look really silly.
It is entirely safe. I have signed a form saying so. Press it, Warden.
A deep note rolls across the mountain. Every stone in Eryri hums back.
The cairn begins to glow, then to shake. The Wardens glance at one another.
Sir. Sir, the floor is making a noise.
That is not in the manual.
The snow on the summit cracks. Something red and enormous rises from under the stone.
Y Ddraig Goch, the Red Dragon, opens one eye. It is the size of a bus. It is deeply unimpressed.
She yawns. The Wardens scatter down the mountain in six directions, shedding lanyards.
This is an unscheduled event. I will be escalating. I will be escalating very quickly, downhill.
Pryce goes after them, his tweed flapping, his spreadsheet clutched to his chest.
Okay. That was not in the brochure. That was not in ANY brochure.
{player}, I thought the Enclosure were the good guys. They had free pens.
Maybe they're not the good guys. Maybe a pen is just a pen.
I'm not going to say anything online. I'm going to sit down. Somewhere with no dragon.
The dragon sinks slowly back into the mountain. The hum fades. For the first time all day, the summit is quiet.
A red feather, or possibly a scale, drifts down and settles on the snow. It is warm.

wyddfa_rangers.text: Yr Wyddfa means 'the grave' or 'the burial mound'. Legend says a giant is buried under the cairn.
It's the highest mountain in England and Wales. Yes, we checked. We got a ruler.

wyddfa_rail.text: The little train goes up there, whistling, from Llanberis. Rack and pinion.
I'm walking down. Tickets are single only. The mountain is also single only.

wyddfa_sheep.text: There are sheep on every ledge. I'm not sure how they're getting up. Or why.
Welsh Mountain sheep: hardy, shy, and unimpressed by lanyards.

wyddfa_photographer.text: I'm waiting for the cloud to lift. I've been here since Tuesday.
The Brocken spectre: sometimes your own shadow turns up in the mist, ringed with a rainbow. I'm hoping.

kit_summit.text: Pryce says he's got a demonstration. I'm filming. That's all I'm doing. Filming.
Go on, talk to him. I'll be here, looking supportive.

kit_summit_after.text: I'm still thinking. That's allowed. It's a new hobby.
Don't tell Mum I said the Enclosure were wrong. She likes the pens.

landsky_wyddfa_geo.text: Sut mae! I'm up here for the rocks, not the view, though the view's thrown in. Do you know what you're standing on? Volcanic ash. Yr Wyddfa is a volcano's leftovers.

About 450 million years ago Wales was under a sea south of the equator, and volcanoes blew ash and lava into it. Between eruptions, sea shells settled on the bottom. So there are fossil shells near the summit of the highest mountain in Wales. Sea floor, a thousand metres up.
Quick one. What carved the great hollows with the lakes in them, Glaslyn and Llyn Llydaw?
options: The sea, when it was higher

then.text: Glaciers. Ice sat in the hollows for thousands of years, grinding them deeper, and left the lakes when it melted. A cwm, we call it; the Scots say corrie. The last ice went about 11,700 years ago.

else.text: It was ice. Glaciers sat in those hollows in the ice ages, grinding them out like a spoon in a pudding, and left the lakes behind. A cwm, we call it. The last of the ice went about 11,700 years ago.

landsky_wyddfa_geo.text: Volcano first, then the sea shells, then the ice, then the railway. In that order. Hwyl!
